desc: Derive and prove the greedy expansion rule: final absorbed segment uniquely determined; order of left/right absorptions doesn't matter.
Build prefix sums and sparse table for O(1) range-argmax queries.
Finalize algorithm design: divide-and-conquer on segment maximum with wall-override mechanism.
Clean up code: dead scaffolding removed; explicit iterative stack avoids recursion-depth issues.

Prove or refute the wall-override value: brute-force cross-validation on 10,000+ small random/adversarial arrays — algorithm matched naive simulation on all cases; proof sketch validated (inner/outer starter dichotomy, propagation, strict inequality).
Analyze total expansion cost: blocker values at least double per crossing → each element visited O(log(maxA)) times; total ~N·30 steps, acceptable for N=5e5.
Handle edge cases: equal values (strict `<`), endpoints, absorption chains — covered in brute-force stress tests (ties, all-equal, sorted, valleys).
Run the full solution end-to-end on both provided samples (exact match) and large-N stress tests (N=2000 vs naive all matched; N=5e5 random/sorted/adversarial/all-equal run in ~1.5–2.6 s).
